mutations.label: a plain route is accepted beside a selected one, declared selected-first
a selected route is accepted beside a plain one, declared plain-first
the table reads the form body to select and does not give it back, so the handler meets an empty form

note: A route selected by a parameter (CloudStack's /client/api?command=...) is a second way of addressing a base pattern, and the table refuses to mix it with the first, in either order, because a request with no command would be answered by whichever the mux preferred. The third mutation is the one that bites only on a POST: the selector lives in the form body, the table must read it to choose a route, and the handler must still find the form after. Without the restore the table is right and every POST is answered as if it carried no parameter at all.
